Measured over the 147 committed `ess` frames, `rear-bracer` clears `pose`'s criterion on 81 of 147 frames at a median visible share of **0.1%** — suppressing the refusal there prints that as READ. ⚠️ **That pair of numbers was taken before the objective interpolated in premultiplied space (§11).** A four-frame spot check on the current objective (`--min-visible 0`, committed `ess` frames `idle/f0000`, `run/f0002`, `walk/f0004`, `aim/f0000`) moved `rear-bracer`'s anchor residual *down* on all four — 0.1564→0.1555, 0.1519→0.1513, 0.1493→0.1488, 0.1537→0.1534 — and flipped its eligibility on none, while `visibleShare` moved materially on one of the four (0.36→0.89). ⇒ Read the **shape** of the row, not those two digits. 🚨 **And that median in particular is one of the ones the `visibleShare` study found unsafe**: `rear-bracer`'s share swings by **0.87** on `idle/f0001` inside `pose`'s own convergence band when the chain anchors on `pose`'s criterion — the basis this figure was taken on. The count and the shape are the reading; the 0.1 % is not a number |
| — | The **other** parts on an anchored bone are refused on their own numbers too, and there they mean something different again: their placement is the **rig's** prediction from that anchor, so their residual is a measurement of the rig (a goggle plate that will not sit on the head it is parented to shows up exactly here) |
| `bone` | the bone this hangs off: its `parent`, its `setupRotationDeg`, its `depth` in links from the anchor, `anchoredTo`, the `dof` searched, the `window` taken, the other parts `sharedWith` it on that bone, and `carriedBones` |
| `bone.dof.pivotFree` | your candidate keys a `translate` timeline on this bone, so the arc this answer sits on has a centre the rig itself moves. The placement is still read off pixels; `localRotationDeg` alone will not reproduce it |
| `bone.carriedBones` | bones between the anchor and here that carry nothing scoreable. Their hinge could not be fitted, their setup rotation was carried through, and every number below them inherits that |
| `bone.pivotDisagreementPx` | anchored bones only: how far the chain's own prediction of this bone's pivot is from where the anchor put it. **This is the one direct measurement of your rig against the picture** — a large value says the joint offset you declared is not the joint the frame shows |
| `anchorVerdict` | what the anchor pass made of this same part: `residual`, `unexplained`, `ambiguous`, `eligible`. ⭐ `eligible: false` beside a `chain` placement is **a part the chain bought** |
| `bone.anchoredToRole` | whether the trunk this hangs off was `anchor` (read off the picture) or `inward` (determined from two anchors below it). ⭐ **The field to check before quoting anything hung off an inward trunk** — that subtree inherits the determination's own uncertainty, and `bone.inward.disagreementPx` on the trunk bone is where it is priced |
| `bone.inward` | non-`null` only on a bone determined inward, and then it is the whole account of that determination — see §12.2b |
| `refusal` | `{ reason, detail }` or `null`. Reasons: `occluded`, `no-match`, `no-anchor`, `no-bracket` (§12.2b), `empty-part`, `no-part-image`, `unsupported-geometry` |

`⚠️ --images is not a part list here.` For `pose` every `.png` in the directory is
a part; for `chainfit` **the candidate decides what the parts are** and the
directory is only where each attachment's image name resolves. Extra PNGs in it are
simply unused; a name the directory lacks is refused `no-part-image` by name.

### 12.4 The flags that steer it

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--anchor <pose.json>` | use this `rigc pose` report instead of running one. Refused together with `--scale` / `--rotation`, which size the internal pass that then does not happen |
| `--atlas` | **refused by name.** Every other `--candidate` command takes it, so trying it here is reasonable — but the part art comes from `--images` and the skeleton is all this needs of the candidate, so a flag that silently did nothing would be worse than one that says why |
| `--hinge <min,max>` | the window each child's local rotation is searched over, in Spine degrees about its setup value. Default `-180,180` — **a full turn, on purpose**: one degree of freedom is cheap enough to sweep exhaustively, and §11.4's warning about a window that does not contain the truth applies here too. The hinge step `3°` is a **ceiling** on the step, not the step: a window it does not divide is divided into whole steps no coarser than it, and `search` states the step that division produced, so `--hinge -20,20` prints `hinge -20°–20° step 2.857° (15 rungs)` and each chain part's note says it was searched `in 2.857° steps`. The full turn divides it exactly |
| `--stretch <ratio>` | also search a uniform bone scale, this ratio either way. Without it, stretch is searched **only where your own animations key a `scale` timeline on that bone** — a rig that never scales a bone is a rig saying that bone does not stretch |
| `--min-visible <0..1>` | below this visible share a placement is refused `occluded` instead of reported flat (default `0.25`). A reporting threshold, not a pass bar; the placement is still in the JSON. ⚠️ **It is not inert, though**: a bone whose frozen share is under this floor gets one *unmasked* look before its visible set is fixed, so the flag also changes **where parts land** and not only which rows are refused. Two runs at different `--min-visible` are two fits, and their shares are not one column |
| `--max-residual <0..1>` | as §11, over the visible pixels (default `0.25`) |
| `--passes <n>` | how many times the masks are rebuilt from the answers and the fit rerun (default `2`). ⚠️ **It buys convergence of the mask onto the answer, and it costs determinacy.** Each pass re-seeds the hinge search on the previous pass's answer, so two nearby inputs that fell into different basins on pass 1 are *further* apart after pass 2. Measured over the 147 committed `ess` frames, the share of readings whose `visibleShare` moves by more than 0.10 under a perturbation inside `pose`'s convergence band runs **0.78 % → 5.45 % → 15.17 %** at `--passes` 1 → 2 → 4. Raise it to settle a `visibleShareAtFit` drift on one frame; do not raise it expecting steadier numbers across runs |
| `--anchor-residual <0..1>` | the residual a `pose` placement must be within to anchor (default `0.16`) |
| `--inward-lever <px>` | how far apart two anchored descendants must sit before the rotation they determine is printed (default `8`). Derived, not picked: a pivot error of ε px across a lever of L px is an angle error of about ε/L radians, so half a pixel inside 3° needs 9.5 px. Below it, `no-bracket` names the measured lever |
| `--scale`, `--rotation` | passed to the **internal anchor pass**, meaning exactly what they mean to `pose` |

### 12.5 What it cannot see — read this before using the numbers

- 🚨 **The occlusion is your candidate's, and so is the geometry.** A wrong draw
  order masks the wrong pixels. A joint offset the rig gets wrong moves the pivot
  every hinge below it turns about. An answer here is only as good as the structure
  it was read through, and that is a different failure mode from anything in §11 —
  `pose` can be wrong about a part, `chainfit` can be wrong about a *limb*, in a
  way that looks internally consistent. `pivotDisagreementPx` and
  `bone.carriedBones` are the two fields that expose it.
- ⚠️ **`residual` here and `residual` in a `pose` report are not the same
  measurement on an occluded part**, by construction: one drops the covered pixels
  and the other charges them. Do not put them in one column. What *is* comparable
  is each against its own `visibleShare` / `unexplained`.
- 🚨 **`visibleShare` cannot be averaged across frames or across fits.** It is
  measured through the fitted placements of the parts drawn over this one, so two
  fits `pose` itself cannot tell apart give it different values — measured: p99
  0.56 and a worst corpus-median move of 22 points inside `pose`'s own polish
  floor. Read it per frame beside its own residual. If a corpus statistic is
  needed, a **maximum** is the one that survives (it saturates), and it should be
  quoted with its spread. §12.3 carries the figures;
  [`bench/studies/2026-09-03-visibleshare`](https://github.com/rig-c/core/blob/main/bench/studies/2026-09-03-visibleshare/README.md)
  carries the method.
- ⚠️ **Setup draw order, on one frame.** A `drawOrder` timeline reorders your slots
  at runtime and this cannot know the time, so a candidate that has one is masked in
  the order its setup pose declares. The report says so in `caveats` when it finds
  one.
- ⚠️ **The hinge is searched; the pivot is not.** Nothing here searches a bone's
  translation, so a bone you key `translate` on is reported `pivotFree` rather than
  solved.
- ⬆️ **The inward step determines a bone; it does not measure one.** §12.2b is the
  whole account. The two things it structurally cannot do: attribute a
  disagreement to one determinant, and reach a bone that does not branch.
- **A constraint moves bones after their local transforms compose.** With IK,
  transform, path or physics constraints in the candidate, a fitted
  `localRotationDeg` is still a placement but not necessarily a value you can key
  and reproduce. The report lists the constraints it found.
- **Shear, a non-uniform scale and any `inherit` but `normal`** are refused
  `unsupported-geometry` by bone, and a non-region attachment by attachment.
  Composing through them would put a plausible number on geometry this instrument
  does not model — the same shape of wrongness as a search window that excludes the
  truth.
- **Nothing here grades anything either.** Same phase as §11, same reason: the pose
  is a given condition and once your spec states it there is nothing left to be
  close to. Every threshold in the report is a reporting threshold. There is no pass
  bar and `caveats` says so in the file.

## 13. Asking the picture a question — `rigc inspect`

The gate answers everything a number can say, and a geometric judgement is not
one of those: *the bones around the head look odd* is a sentence about a picture.
`inspect` draws that picture of a green build — the art, and over it the rig's own
geometry at one moment — and writes a **legend** beside it that turns every mark
back into world units. The picture is for reading; the legend is for acting on what
was read, because a position taken off it goes straight into a spec.

```bash
bun cli.ts inspect --candidate gallery/look/build --show art,bones,names --dim --max 640 --out look.png
# rigc inspect
#   ..    skeleton …/gallery/look/build/skeleton.json
#   ..    atlas    …/gallery/look/build/skeleton.atlas
#   ..    poser    rigc core — …/skeleton.model.json
#   ..    view     art,bones,names over dimmed art — the setup pose
#   ..    box      world x -35.2..835.2, y -35.2..915.2 at 0.6734 px per unit — 1 tile(s) of 586x640px (exact in the legend)
# rigc: wrote …/look.png
# rigc: wrote …/look.json
```

It poses through the poser `render` would pose the candidate with, and the `poser`
line says which — rigc's core for a build with its `skeleton.model.json`, spine-core
for an export or a named fallback (the `--poser` row in §0). Without `--zoom` or
`--viewport` the picture is framed exactly as `render` frames the build at the same
`--max`, so with nothing drawn over it the art **is** `render`'s frame, pixel for
pixel (`IN09`).

### 13.1 Which question, which view

| The question | The view | What to read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Is this bone where the art is? | `--show art,bones,names --dim` | each bone as a line from its origin to its tip, the origin a filled square, the tip a hollow one; a bone of length 0 is a hollow 5x5 square around its origin, so a joint nobody gave a length is not mistaken for a point on another bone. Three fringe chains drawn as evenly spaced page verticals is the kind of thing this shows at a glance |
| Which way does this bone squash? | `--show art,axes --zoom <bone>` | the bone's world **x** axis (red) and **y** axis (green), each 24 px long at a world scale of 1 — longer or shorter as the bone scales. A `scaley` key squashes along the green one; if that is the page's vertical on a face painted at an angle, the blink squashes along the page |
| Where in rig units is this point? | `--show art,grid --zoom <bone or slot>` or `--viewport x,y,w,h` | grid lines at whole multiples of a step in **world units**, each labelled with its value, the lines through 0 darker. The legend's transform converts any pixel exactly; the grid is for reading by eye |
| Is this axis declared, and held? | `--show art,declared,bones` | each `invariants.axes` line (§3.7) through its two bones' origins, drawn across the whole tile, and the bones it holds drawn in their own colour; the legend states each held bone's world x axis and how far off the line it lies, as `A51` measures it, at the pose drawn |
| Did it break during the move? | any of the above `--animation <name> --at <s,s,…>` | one tile per time, left to right on one grid, each labelled with its time and frame |
| What does this bone move? | `--show art,mesh,weights:<bone> --dim` | the bone's weight over every region and mesh it moves, as a heat: a pixel whose centre lies in a triangle is painted the ramp's colour at the blend of its corners' weights — blue near 0, yellow at 0.5, red at 1 (the stops are in the legend) — and a weight of 0 is not painted, so the art shows where the bone does not reach. A region and an unweighted mesh are moved whole by their slot's bone. The weights are read off `skeleton.json`, the file both posers skin from; a bone that weights nothing paints nothing and the run says so on a line of its own |
| Does this part's edge follow that bone? | `--show art,weights:<bone>,mesh --overlay-slot <part> --zoom slot:<part>` | the part's own triangles and the bone's weight over them alone, over the whole painting. Where slots stack — a neck under the face, the hair, a collar — every mesh crossing the box is drawn and the heat is the union of every slot the bone moves, so the part's edge has no pixel of its own until the others are left out. The legend's `meshes[]` gives the part's weight for the bone at every vertex, so "does the top row follow the head" is read as numbers as well as colour |
| Is this rig's density where its motion is? | `--show art,density --dim` | each region and mesh filled by its **ratio** — its triangles per world unit² over the figure's — on one ramp, log-scaled and centred on 1×: grey is as dense as the figure, pink to magenta denser (4×, 16×), light to dark green sparser (1/4×, 1/16×), clamped past the end stops (the stops are in the legend). A part's area is its posed mesh's own, the sum of its triangles' areas at the pose drawn, not the image's box; a region is two triangles over its quad. Where parts overlap the pixel is the part drawn last, as in the art, so a part under others is read with `--overlay-slot <part>`. The figure's totals are always over every slot the pose shows — the filter picks what is drawn and listed, never what the figure is — and the legend's `density` gives each slot's attachment, kind, vertices, triangles, hull, area, triangles per area, ratio and the bones it is weighted to, in draw order. A measurement, not a verdict: no bar is drawn, and `A13_MESH_BUDGET` stays the one gate on counts |
| Does a joint tear in this animation? | `render --seam <a>:<b> --animation <name>` (§8.8) | One line per pair: the frames where background opens inside the joint (gap) or the overlap band of one piece shows past its partner (ghost), with the worst frame's cell count and world box; `seam.json` carries every frame and its time, and the runs of frames. A pair whose drawings never overlap is a SKIP, said by name. A reading, not a verdict — the exit status never moves |
| Which slot covers which in this animation? | `render --overlaps --animation <name>` (§8.9) | One `OVERLAP "<under>" under "<over>"` line per pair that moves: the frames it covers on, as runs, and the most pixels it covers and the frame of them; one line counting the layering the motion does not move. `overlaps.json` carries every frame's pairs with their pixel count and box, and `overlaps-f<NNNN>.png` draws each covered frame's contours, the covered part dashed. A reading, not a verdict — the draw-order key is the remedy |
| Does anything fold in this animation? | `render --folds --animation <name>` (§8.3), then `inspect --show art,folds,mesh --animation <name> --at <the worst frame's time> --zoom folds` | `render --folds` prints one line per mesh with a triangle turned over against the setup pose: the frames, the worst frame's count, which triangles, their world box at that frame and their setup-pose area. The view fills those triangles at the pose drawn — every pixel whose centre a folded triangle holds — in the colour the legend's `folds` states, and the legend's `folds[]` names, per mesh, the folded triangles by index with the same box and area, and the setup pose's degenerate and inverted ones, which are never counted. A fold is usually a sliver a few units across, invisible in a picture of the whole mesh: `--zoom folds` frames the picture to the folded triangles' box. A thin sliver still needs pixels — raise `--max` when the fill is a line. A reading, not a verdict |
| How is this part triangulated? | `--show art,mesh,hull --zoom slot:<slot>` | each mesh's triangle edges, and over them its hull — vertex 0 to 1 to … to `hull − 1` and back. Regions are not drawn: a region is not a mesh. The legend lists every vertex in world units and in pixels |
| Which is drawn over which? | `--show art,slots` | each slot that shows a region or mesh numbered by its place in the draw order **at the pose drawn** (0 is drawn first), on a white box at the centre of its attachment's box — so a `drawOrder` key (§4.7) shows from the first frame `render` draws it on |
| Did this change move anything? | `--compare <dir>` beside any view | the same view of a second build beside the first, at the same times, on **one** world box and one transform, each half labelled `A`/`B` with the poser that posed it. A mark on a different pixel in the two halves is at a different place in the two rigs |

### 13.2 Where it looks

- **The setup pose** by default.
- **One time, or several** — `--animation <name> --at <s[,s…]>`. A time is a frame
  of the grid `render --fps <n>` draws the animation on (default 12): the pose at
  `--at 0.5` is `render`'s `f0006.png`, the same continuous trajectory stepped the
  same way, physics included. A time off that grid is refused naming the frames
  either side (`--at 0.3 is not on the 12 fps frame grid … the frames either side
  are 3 (0.2500s) and 4 (0.3333s)`); pass `--fps` for another grid. A time past the
  end is refused naming the animation's length. Several times are a sheet: tiles
  left to right, eight to a row, a one-pixel rule between them, all on one world box
  so a mark that moves between two tiles moved in the rig.
- **The whole rig**, framed as `render` frames it; **a box** — `--viewport x,y,w,h`
  in world units, y up, `x,y` its bottom-left corner; or **one bone or slot** —
  `--zoom <name>[:<pad>]`, the bone's origin and tip or the slot's attachment
  vertices over every time drawn, padded by `<pad>` world units on every side
  (default a quarter of the box's longer side). A name that is both a bone and a slot
  is refused until it is written `bone:<name>` or `slot:<name>`; a bone of length 0
  with no pad is one point, and is refused asking for one. **The folds** —
  `--zoom folds[:<pad>]`: the box of every triangle folded over (§8.3) at the times
  drawn, in every mesh `--overlay-slot`/`--hide-overlay-slot` keep — the union of
  the legend's `folds[].box` over the tiles — padded as above. With nothing folded at
  those times it is refused, naming the meshes that fold on the animation's grid and
  their frames (`--zoom folds: nothing to frame — no mesh has a triangle folded over
  at t=1s of "turn" — at 12 fps these do: "hair_lock_l" on frame(s) [22-23], worst
  frame 22 (t=1.8333s); …`); at the setup pose — what a fold is read against —
  nothing folds, and it says so. A rig with a bone or slot named `folds` is refused
  until the name is written `bone:folds` or `slot:folds`.
- **Two builds** — `--compare <dir | skeleton.json>`. The second build is loaded as
  the first is (its own poser, chosen by what it carries, on a `poser    B:` line),
  posed at the same times, and drawn beside it: one time is two halves side by side,
  several are pairs, four to a row. The box is the one `--viewport` names, or the
  union of what `--zoom` names in **both** builds, or — with neither — the union of
  `render`'s framing of each, so a half is `render`'s frame of its build only where
  the two framings agree. A name either build lacks is refused naming that build.
- `--max` is each tile's longer side in pixels (default 256), as on `render`.
- `--dim` fades the art toward white (each channel keeps 0.4 of its distance from
  white) so what is drawn over it reads.

### 13.3 Labels, and which bones and slots are drawn

- **One label per pixel.** Bones whose origins land on one pixel — a `_ctl` bone and
  its identity child, a chain's joint — are one label: the first by declaration
  order, then `+N` for the rest (`leg0_ctl +2`). The pixel is the unit because it is
  what overprints: two origins a third of a pixel apart print their names on each
  other as surely as two that coincide. The legend's `labels` lists every bone of
  each label, and `bones` keeps every bone.
- **No label over another.** Labels are placed in declaration order (slot numbers
  first); one that would touch an earlier label moves down a text line at a time
  until it is clear, and a grey leader joins it to its origin. After 16 lines it
  stays where it began and the legend marks it `overlaps`.
- **`--bone <glob[,glob…]>`** draws only the bones a pattern matches, and
  **`--hide-bone <glob[,glob…]>`** none of the ones it matches, applied after
  `--bone` — so `--bone 'bang_*' --hide-bone '*_ctl,*_px'` is the fringe chains
  without their control bones. A pattern is a glob — `*` any run of characters, `?`
  one, matched against the whole name — rather than a regular expression: bone names
  are identifiers, the patterns are comma-separated, and a glob needs no escaping in
  the shell. The filter is on `bones`, `axes` and `names`; every bone stays in the
  legend, and a left-out one says which flag left it out in `undrawn`. A pattern
  that matches no bone is refused naming the bones there are.
- **`--overlay-slot <glob[,glob…]>`** draws the per-slot views — `mesh`, `hull`,
  `weights:<bone>`, `density`, `folds` and `slots` — only for the slots a pattern matches, and
  **`--hide-overlay-slot <glob[,glob…]>`** for none of the ones it matches, applied
  after `--overlay-slot`; the patterns are globs, as `--bone`'s are. The **art is not
  filtered**: the painting is what the edge is read against, and `--dim` already
  quiets it, and neither is the figure a `density` is measured against. A slot left
  out is absent from `meshes[]`, `slots[]` and the density rows, and a slot kept
  keeps its number — its place in the whole draw order, not among the slots drawn. A
  pattern that matches no slot is refused naming the slots there are. It is not
  `--slot`: on `render` that flag draws a subset of the *art*, by exact name, which is
  the opposite of what this keeps whole.

### 13.4 The legend

`<out>.json` beside `<out>.png`, `rigc-inspect/1`. What it states:

- `coordinates` — the two spaces and the transform, in both directions, as text:
  `px = x0 + (x - minX) * scale; py = y0 + (maxY - y) * scale` and
  `x = minX + (px - x0) / scale; y = maxY - (py - y0) / scale`. World is Spine's, y up;
  the picture is y down from its top-left corner, and pixel (i, j) covers
  `[i, i+1) x [j, j+1)` — a position's pixel is its floor.
- `viewport` — the world box every tile is a picture of and its size in pixels;
  `size` — the whole picture's.
- `tiles[]` — per tile: `animation`, `frame` and `time` (`frame / fps`), its `box` in
  the picture, its own `transform` (`minX`, `maxY`, `scale`, and `x0`, `y0`, its
  top-left pixel), and `bones[]` — every bone in declaration order with its
  `parent`, `length`, `zeroLength`, `origin` and `tip` each as `{ world, pixel }`,
  `undrawn` (why it is not drawn — its world matrix is 0 at this time, unposed by the
  skin or scaled to 0, or a `--bone`/`--hide-bone` pattern left it out — or `null`),
  and with `axes` shown, the two axis ends. With `grid`, the step and every line's
  value; with `declared`, each entry's line in degrees, its two points, and each held
  bone's angle and how far off the line it is. With `names`, `labels[]`: each label's
  `text`, the `bones` it stands for, its `anchor` pixel, the `box` it is drawn in,
  and whether it was `moved` or `overlaps`. With `density`, `density`: the
  `figure` at this tile's pose — `slots`, `triangles`, `area` (world units²) and
  `trianglesPerArea`, over every slot whose attachment is a region or mesh — and
  `slots[]`, one row per kept slot in draw order: `order`, `slot`, `attachment`,
  `kind`, `alpha`, `vertices`, `triangles`, `hull`, `area`, `trianglesPerArea`,
  `ratio`, the `rgba` it is painted, `bones` (how many bones it is weighted to —
  a region's or an unweighted mesh's is its slot's one) and `boneNames`. A part
  whose posed area is 0 has `trianglesPerArea` and `ratio` `null` and says why in
  `why`; it is not painted. With `folds`, `folds[]`: every kept mesh with a
  triangle folded at this tile's pose or a setup fault, in draw order — `slot`,
  `attachment`, `triangleCount`, `folded` (the triangles filled, by index),
  `degenerate` and `inverted` (the setup pose's, never counted), `box` (the folded
  triangles' world box at this pose, `[minX, minY, maxX, maxY]`; `null` when none is
  folded), `area` (their setup-pose area, world units²) and `share` (that over the
  mesh's setup-pose area) — §8.3's numbers; empty when none.
  With `mesh`, `hull`, `weights`, `density` or `folds`,
  `meshes[]`: every region and mesh the pose shows, in draw order, with its `kind`,
  `vertexCount`, `triangleCount`, `hull` (a mesh's hull vertex count), its unique
  triangle `edges` as vertex pairs, every posed vertex in `world` and `pixel`, and
  with `weights` the bone's weight at each vertex. With `slots`, `slots[]`: each
  slot's `order`, `slot`, `attachment`, `bone`, its `anchor` and number's `box`.
  On a sheet or a compare, `label` — the tile's label text and box; with `--compare`,
  `build` — `A` or `B`.
- `colours` — every colour the picture draws, as RGBA, with what it means.
- `poser`, `show`, `dim`, `skin`, `animation`, `fps` and `framing` — what was drawn
  and how it was framed (`shot`, `zoom` with the bone or slot — or with `folds`, what
  the box is of — the pad and whether it was stated, or `viewport`).
- `weights` — with `weights:<bone>`: the bone, the ramp's stops as RGBA, the floor
  below which nothing is painted, and how a pixel's weight is read.
- `density` — with `density`: the ramp's stops (`ratio`, RGBA), the `scale` it is
  read on (log₂ of the ratio, clamped at the end stops), and in words what `area`,
  the figure's `totals` and the `ratio` are and how a pixel is painted.
- `folds` — with `folds`: the colour a folded triangle is filled with, as RGBA, and
  what it means; `degenerateShare` (2⁻³⁰, §8.3); and in words what `folded`,
  `degenerate` and `inverted` are, how a triangle is named by `index`, and what
  `box` and `area` are. Its colour
  is stated here rather than in `colours`, which every legend lists whole, so a legend
  drawn without `folds` is the bytes it was before the view existed.
- `boneFilter` — `--bone` and `--hide-bone` as given.
- `slotFilter` — `--overlay-slot` and `--hide-overlay-slot` as given; with it,
  `meshes[]` and `slots[]` list only the slots it keeps.
- `builds` — with `--compare`: each build (`A`, `B`), the poser that posed it, and
  its `skeleton.json`'s sha256. `poser` is build `A`'s.

Every number is `JSON.stringify`'s, the double the pose produced, not a rounding of
it. The same build and flags write the same bytes (`IN10`).

### 13.5 What it refuses

Each of these exits 2, writes nothing, and names what exists: a bone or slot the
build does not have (both rosters listed), an animation or skin it does not declare,
a `--show` word it does not draw, a flag it does not take, a time off the frame grid
or past the end, `--at` without `--animation` and the reverse, `--zoom` beside
`--viewport`, `--show declared` on a skeleton with no `skeleton.model.json`
beside it whose `spine.sha256` is its own — a Spine export states no rig invariants —
`weights` with no bone or with a bone the build lacks (the bones listed), a
`--bone`/`--hide-bone` pattern that matches no bone (the bones listed), an
`--overlay-slot`/`--hide-overlay-slot` pattern that matches no slot (the slots
listed), `--zoom folds` with no triangle folded over at the times drawn (the meshes
that fold on the grid and their frames listed), and, with
`--compare`, any of these that holds of the second build, said as `the --compare
build: …` — except `--zoom folds`, which frames to whichever build folds and is
refused only when neither does, each build's frames named.
A rig that declares no `invariants.axes` is not refused: the picture draws nothing
for `declared` and the run says so on a line of its own.

### 13.6 What it is not

- **Not a score.** Nothing in it is a pass bar; the picture is read, and what is read
  is acted on in the spec.
- **Not a player.** It is one still, or a sheet of stills. A person watches
  `@rig-c/play` or `rigc preview`.
- **Not a second poser.** Everything it draws is a pose `render` would have drawn at
  the same frame; where it disagrees with `render --geometry`, it is wrong (`IN04`).

## 14. Read a named mesh at setup

`rig-c/core` promises `readSetupMesh(view, target)` and the types
`SetupMeshTarget` and `SetupMesh` (issue #1538). It reads any named mesh or linked
mesh, including one the setup pose does not select, without a player, animation
step or change to the document's setup selection.

```ts
import { readModel, underNoSkin, readSetupMesh } from 'rig-c/core';
import type { SetupMeshTarget, SetupMesh } from 'rig-c/core';

const view = underNoSkin(readModel(modelText));
const target: SetupMeshTarget = { slot: 'flag', attachment: 'alternate' };
const mesh: SetupMesh = readSetupMesh(view, target);
// mesh.vertices: full-double world x,y pairs, y up; no crop/camera conversion.
```

| field | contract |
| --- | --- |
| `target.slot`, `target.attachment` | exact slot name and attachment **table key**; a record's display name, path or atlas region is not an alias |
| `target.skin` omitted | retain the supplied view, including `readModel`'s `all`; use `underNoSkin` for a fresh skeleton's view |
| `target.skin: null` | no skin set: default-table fallback, no skin-required bones or constraints activated |
| `target.skin: name` | the named view, with default-table fallback; only the named skin's activation lists apply |
| `target.skin: 'all'` | all activation lists; a uniquely filled key resolves, identical definitions keep the existing resolver's first supplying skin, differing definitions are refused because the model does not carry the Spine file's merge order |
| `mesh.slot`, `mesh.attachment`, `mesh.skin` | requested slot and table key, and the table's supplying skin (which can be the default fallback); a linked mesh retains its own identity |
| `mesh.vertices` | fresh mutable `number[]`, flat x,y in world units; stored coordinates and weights use the poser's float32 reading and influence order, without normalization |
| `mesh.triangles`, `mesh.hull` | fresh mutable triangle indices; hull is the number of leading hull **vertices**, or `null` when absent |

Definition equality ignores object property insertion order at every depth,
including weighted binding records. Array positions, object key presence and
leaf values remain significant; leaves use `Object.is`, so positive and negative
zero are distinct when retained in a model. Reordering object keys alone is not
a different definition. A genuine value, shape or array-order difference still
produces the same named all-skin refusal; no merge order is inferred.

The setup matrices come from the raw setup poser's existing constraint path,
including setup sliders and reset physics. A selected mesh is bit-identical to
`poseRawSetup(view)`'s geometry, including any setup-slider deform. An unselected
mesh uses its stored vertices through those same matrices: the API never switches
an attachment to ask what a slider or path constraint would do after a switch.
A linked mesh borrows its source vertices, triangles and hull; unweighted
vertices use the queried slot's bone, weighted vertices their named bindings.
Its `timelines` flag controls source-deform inheritance only when selected, as
in the existing setup poser. An inactive bone keeps the existing zero world
matrix; an attachment read does not activate it.

Every result is detached: changing its object or arrays changes no document,
pose, cached topology or subsequent read. Missing slots, attachments and skins,
and region, clipping, path or bounding-box targets, throw `CoreInputError`
naming the requested identity and the problem. Examples include
`setup mesh slot "s" attachment "missing" under skin null: no such attachment`
and `…: region is not a mesh`. Ambiguous all-skin definitions name their skins
and say `choose a named skin`; unknown skin retains `underSkin`'s existing
`--skin "missing": no such skin` refusal. Existing setup/non-finite refusals
propagate; the read does not manufacture a partial result when setup is absent.

`S1538` controls exercise literal coordinates, detached data, linked meshes,
skin lookup and activation, setup-slider deform, and the official runtime's
`computeWorldVertices` using ordinary JS output arrays at tolerance 0. The
runtime stores local mesh coordinates and weights in float32, but an output
`Float32Array` would add a second rounding that this API does not perform.

**Measured nonselected slider distinction.** In spine-core 4.3.13,
`computeWorldVertices(skeleton, slot, …)` over an unselected mesh still reads
the **selected slot's deform array**, even for a linked mesh with
`timelines: false`. `S1538_09` measures a slider at time 0.5 interpolating
local offsets `(1,2)` and `(3,4)` to `(2,3)`, with a selected source mesh,
a linked mesh inheriting its timeline, and an independent linked mesh.
All three selected reads are exact. Four of the six nonselected calls to the
official method reuse the selected deform; their maximum absolute difference
from this API is `2.9999999999999982` world units. The other two nonselected
calls, with the independent linked mesh selected, agree exactly. The API's
nonselected output is the stored source geometry through the unchanged setup
matrices; it does not borrow a different selection's deform. The control
checks both results and the source of the difference, without an epsilon.

## 15. Posing in place for a player — the runtime poser (stage 0)

rigc poses a model document twice over, on purpose (issue #1591). The **oracle**
(`src/core/`) is the reference: each pose is a pure function of the document,
the skin and the time, returned as a fresh, name-keyed, detached record, and it
is the poser `tools/core_gate.ts` holds to spine-core 4.3.13 at tolerance 0. The
**runtime poser** (`src/runtime/`) is for a player drawing many skeletons a
frame: it resolves every name to an index once at load and overwrites typed
arrays in place, so a steady-state frame allocates nothing. It computes every
value with the oracle's own formulas in the oracle's order of operations, and it
is held equal to the oracle at tolerance 0 rather than trusted; the oracle is not
changed for it. It is imported from `rig-c/runtime`, an **experimental** entry
(RELEASING.md, *The import surface*): not promised until it stabilises, so a
minor may reshape it and a dependant pins an exact version.

```ts
import { readModel, underNoSkin } from 'rig-c/core';
import { compileRuntime, RuntimePose, RuntimeRefusal } from 'rig-c/runtime'; // experimental

const view = underNoSkin(readModel(modelText));
const model = compileRuntime(view, { ignore: ['events'] }); // throws RuntimeRefusal, every missing construct named
const pose = new RuntimePose(model);                         // every buffer allocated here, once
pose.setAnimation('walk');                                   // a refused animation throws its RuntimeRefusal
pose.step(1 / 60);                                           // or pose.apply(t) at an animation time
pose.computeVertices();
// pose.world: 6 numbers per bone (a, b, c, d, worldX, worldY — W_A … W_Y), y up
// pose.light: 4 per slot; pose.shown: per slot an index into model.attachments, or −1
// pose.vertices: model.attachments[i].count numbers at model.attachments[i].offset
```

| | what stage 0 poses |
| --- | --- |
| bones | local and world transforms, all five inherit modes, skin-required bones under the view's skin (an inactive bone is zeros, as the oracle poses it) |
| timelines | `rotate`, `translate(x/y)`, `scale(x/y)`, `shear(x/y)`; a slot's `attachment`, `rgba`, `rgb` and `alpha`; ik and transform timelines; linear, stepped and Bézier keys, each read from a per-pose key cursor |
| constraints | one- and two-bone ik; world-space, absolute transform constraints; the document's order, each followed by the bones below what it moved posed again |
| vertices | regions, meshes, weighted meshes and linked meshes, written into the pose's buffer |
| time | one animation at full weight from the setup pose, at a time (`apply`) or stepped as a looping track (`step`, the track time wrapped by the duration as `openTrack` wraps it) |

**Everything else is refused at load, by name.** `RuntimeRefusal.missing` lists
every construct met, each `{ feature, detail, animation }`, and the message
reads `not posed by the runtime poser (stage 0), N construct(s) missing:
<feature>: <detail>; …`. A model-level feature refuses the whole model; an
animation-level one refuses that animation alone (`model.refused`;
`model.animation(name)` and `setAnimation(name)` throw its refusal) and every
other animation is posed. Fall back to the oracle (`openTrack`) for what is
refused: nothing is posed approximately.

| feature | refuses | what it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `skin` | the model | a skin other than `default` |
| `path-constraint`, `physics-constraint`, `slider-constraint` | the model | a constraint of that kind |
| `local-transform`, `additive-transform` | the model | a transform constraint with `localSource` or `localTarget`, or `additive` |
| `inactive-constrained-bone` | the model | an applied ik or transform constraint naming a bone the view leaves inactive (what the oracle writes there depends on the pass before) |
| `noscale-world-target` | the model | a world-space transform onto a `noScale` or `noScaleOrReflection` bone, whose local values would be read back in that mode |
| `clipping`, `null-atlas-region` | the model when shown at setup, else the animation that keys it | a clipping attachment; a region whose atlas rectangle the model states as `null` |
| `skin-conflict` | as above | a placeholder the skins fill differently |
| `oracle-absent` | the model | a pose the oracle itself leaves out (`constraintsAbsentWhy`) |
| `inherit-timeline`, `deform-timeline`, `sequence-timeline`, `draw-order-timeline`, `dark-colour-timeline` | the animation | a timeline of that kind (`dark-colour` is `rgba2` / `rgb2`) |
| `events` | the animation, unless `ignore: ['events']` | event keys. Events move no pose, so a consumer that reads none may ask for them to be ignored and is handed a poser that fires none; without the request a dropped cue would be silent |

A call it cannot answer throws `RuntimeInputError`, naming the call:
`apply: no animation is set (setAnimation first)`, `animation "x" is not one of
this document's [...]`, `apply: the time NaN is not finite`.

**The gate.** `tools/core_gate.ts` runs a third dumper (`runtimeDump` in
`tools/pose_oracle.ts`) over every row it builds, at the oracle's samples, and
compares its document with the oracle's in full doubles at tolerance 0 twice:
through `compare` and cell by cell (which reads the bones `compare`'s
ill-conditioned rule leaves out). One `RUNTIME` line per row reads `IDENTICAL`
(covered whole and equal), `SKIP` (refused at load, or animations or events left
out — every one named), `DIFF` (the first value that differs) or `REFUSED`; then
one `RUNTIME SKIP feature <name>` line per feature with the rows it refused, a
`HOLE` line when no row is covered whole or nothing was compared, and `RUNTIME
GREEN|RED`, counting rows covered whole, covered in part and refused at load, and
the poses and values compared. A `DIFF` or `REFUSED` turns the run RED; a SKIP
never counts as a pass. The page UVs are the atlas's and are compared by neither
side here. The selftest's `runtime-poser` suite holds the gate to its plants (a
1e-6° bone perturbation, a weighted binding bound to the wrong bone index, a
refused feature smuggled through — each caught by name), a seeded population of
every construct above, the looping step against `openTrack`, and a steady-state
frame measured at 0 bytes with the collector off.
